home.metaDescription: Jaeung Kim, a frontend developer in Seoul.
paragraphs: I care about how a screen feels. I like refining the flow of a product until people move through it without thinking about it.
Simple on the surface, precise underneath. That is the balance I chase, and the problems along the way are the fun part.
Off work I play basketball and spend time outdoors to recharge.
This site is my workshop. I use it to try things I want to learn, test small ideas, and keep notes on ordinary days.

resume.metaDescription: Resume of Jaeung Kim, frontend engineer, with experience, projects, skills, and education.
resume.name: Jaeung (Jae) Kim
intro: I am a frontend engineer with five years of experience. I currently work on an automotive R&D platform that models large engineering datasets as an ontology and visualizes them as a knowledge graph, so thousands of spreadsheets and PDFs from across departments can be searched in plain language and traced to their source.
In a complex domain, interface design decides the outcome. I start by observing how users respond and refine the UI/UX from there. A good screen makes the next step obvious without explanation.

I hold my code to the same standard. I design consistent structures that the next developer can use immediately and document the reasoning behind them. On my current project I own the frontend architecture and work with designers and backend engineers from planning onward to shape the product and the frontend. Translating between design intent and implementation is the work I do best.

I adopt new tools such as AI quickly, but adoption is not the goal. I focus on designing how people and AI work together and making that a shared team standard. An environment the whole team uses well matters more than one person using it well.

e8ight.platformHeading: Frontend platform standardization and developer environment
platformBullets: Consolidated the shared UI package, Storybook design system, lint and i18n templates, and branching strategy into one monorepo standard, so new products skip setup and start on domain work
Moved the legacy CRA setup to Vite and a pnpm workspace and introduced a Jenkins and Docker pipeline, cutting CI builds from 10 minutes to under 2 (about 80%)
Deployed Sentry on an internal server to collect every product's error logs in one place and catch incidents through alerts
Enforced lint, type checks, and commit conventions as a commit stage gate, so code from people and coding agents is verified to the same standard
Built a coding agent collaboration environment from 15 custom commands and workflows, role specific subagents, and skills. Now the frontend team standard and spreading to the backend team

hyundai.title: Hyundai Motor R&D data integration platform
hyundai.description: Internal platform that integrates Hyundai Motor R&D data into an ontology based knowledge graph. Led the frontend architecture and built the graph visualization SDK and the LLM chat.
sdkBullets: Designed the knowledge graph visualization SDK shared by the company's GraphRAG products. Split rendering and the d3-force layout into a core with no React dependency, exposed through one imperative handle, so internal rewrites never break call sites

Capped the nodes drawn per screen around a neighborhood based exploration model and dropped WebGL bulk renderers such as sigma.js after evaluation. Within that budget, rendered directly to Canvas 2D, paused rendering when idle, and cached labels as bitmaps to keep interaction smooth
Kept fast changing state in a store outside React and propagated updates only on real data changes, removing needless rerenders in large lists
hyundai.llmHeading: LLM chat integrated with the knowledge graph
llmBullets: Rendered the supporting subgraph on the adjacent canvas from the graph query attached to each GraphRAG answer, so a source can be traced on the graph itself
Routed the WebSocket stream by type into text, reasoning steps, and graph evidence, and decoupled receiving from display with a token queue. Batched chunks per frame to minimize rerenders

Drained the token queue at a steady pace, accelerated when it fell behind, and snapped to the received text on stop or error. Rendered only completed segments as markdown so unclosed code blocks and partial formulas never broke the layout

digitalTwin.title: Digital Twin Federation integrated portal
digitalTwin.description: Integrated portal for a government R&D program: one shell that brings external digital twin tools and partner institutions' deliverables into a single environment. Designed and built as the sole full stack engineer, from the authentication, authorization, and organization model through the Next.js 15 frontend and NestJS backend, and delivered on schedule.
bullets: Designed authentication and authorization as global guards with deny by default, so a new API cannot ship without authentication
Kept tokens in HttpOnly cookies only, never exposed to the browser, with refresh token rotation and reuse detection to block stolen tokens
Gated security settings behind environment variables so one deployment image serves both public HTTPS and internal HTTP

products.title: Company product suite (NAXiS, PMIS, NDX Cloud, and others)
products.description: Led frontend development for five company products.
naxisBullets: A graph editor for building ontologies without code. Kept the domain model (entity types, relations, serialization) separate from React Flow, so other company products adopted it unchanged
Collapsed hubs with hundreds of edges on one node into relation group nodes and merged identical relations into one edge, with partial relayout on expand and collapse instead of a full pass
pmisBullets: Rebuilt a tree of thousands of rows with lazy loading and virtual scrolling, cutting initial load from 12 seconds to 2 (about 80%)
Parallelized serial drawing uploads, taking 19 files from 4 minutes to 20 seconds, with optimistic UI and rollback for instant feedback
ndxCloudBullets: Abstracted four permission levels (organization, project, site, dataset) into one RBAC matrix for consistent access control down to the screen
Cut EXIF extraction for 4,000 images to parsing only the JPEG APP1 marker, taking memory from 20 GB to 800 MB
Uploaded directly from the browser to S3 with presigned URLs, taking 20 minutes down to 10 with 70% less server load

bullets: First developer at a clothing marketplace startup. Owned the stack choice, frontend architecture, deployment, and operations alone
Designed and built the platform that gathers multiple Shopify seller stores into one marketplace. Products and orders stayed in each store, and the platform owned discovery and the buying experience
Kept Supabase Auth as the single identity layer and wired Instagram and TikTok Login Kit on top, so users sign in with a social account while sessions are managed in one place
Chose Shopify Payments over a custom gateway integration, keeping card handling outside the platform while improving cart abandonment and transaction success
EMR (Electronic Medical Records) SaaS startup. Full stack ownership across the marketing site, an internal admin portal, the backend API, and AWS infrastructure
Designed and built the WebGL (Three.js) 3D marketing site alone, from design through implementation and deployment
Designed and built scroll and page transition interactions with GSAP and Framer Motion
Designed and operated the HR and attendance admin portal. Treated non technical executives as the primary users and shaped the screens so they needed no training
Designed and built the Express backend API, MongoDB schema, AWS infrastructure, and CI/CD pipeline
Designed the React component architecture at a cryptocurrency exchange startup. Drew the line between shared components and screen code so new screens were composed from existing pieces
Designed the credit card payment integration and built the crypto purchase flow from card authorization to asset credit
Fixed empty social media previews for SPA links with Lambda@Edge. Injected per route Open Graph meta at the CloudFront edge without changing how the frontend renders
Worked with designers from Figma to improve UI/UX, reconciling design intent and implementation component by component

gantt: Open source Gantt chart on npm for React 18 and 19. Controlled component that persists nothing: once an edit is committed, the complete next task list goes out through a single callback

Calendar, task tree, and timeline geometry are pure modules tested separately from React. Drag, keyboard, and detail panel edits share one commit path, so working day snapping and summary row moves behave the same from every input
Virtualized on both axes, rows and time cells, with five scales from day to year. The bundle imports only React and stays under 40 kB gzipped
No toolbar, just the chart. Scale is driven through an imperative handle and the theme overridden through CSS variables
Move, resize, and reorder tasks from the keyboard, with edits announced to screen readers. English and Korean docs plus a playground
